description: Dependency updates on our own schedule (Chapter 20): Renovate opens no pull requests. It keeps one
issue - the dependency dashboard - listing what is out of date; updates are made by hand once a month,
after reading the release notes: patch versions together in one pull request, every minor or major
version in one per component (the chart with the tool that tests it).
Versions outside a standard file carry a '# renovate: datasource=... depName=...' comment above them.
Vulnerability alerts stay with GitHub's own alerts (on for the repository); the workflow token cannot read them.

customManagers.description: Versions pinned in Terraform variables, tfvars, the Makefile, CI workflows and Flux manifests (where no standard manager reads them), each under a '# renovate:' comment.

packageRules.description: The platform's own images are updated by Flux image automation, not here.

description: origin-ca-issuer's CRDs come from its Git repository pinned by commit (flux/bootstrap/components/public-edge/public-edge.yaml).
Renovate would follow the default branch's HEAD, not the release tags; the chart version (helm datasource) is the signal
for a new release, and the CRD commit is moved to that release's tag by hand, in the same pull request.
